visual_distinctiveness: The deck runs a committed two-tone system (dark navy alternating with cream across slides) plus a gold accent, and deploys a recurring italic-gold word in every action title (e.g., '$47.2M' in slide-02, 'customs declined 15.8%' in slide-03, 'not yet profitable' in slide-07). This clear point of view and consistent execution warrants a base of 4. However, the small gold horizontal rule that appears under every section label (visible below 'THE QUARTER IN ONE LINE' on slide-02, 'SEGMENT DETAIL' on slide-03, 'GROSS MARGIN BRIDGE' on slide-05, and every other interior slide) is a decorative accent line carrying no information, triggering the automatic −1 deduction per the rubric. No other deductions apply: backgrounds alternate (not flat uniform), palette is navy-dominant (not timid), no ornamental icons, no workflow metadata. Base 4 − 1 = 3.

Committed navy/cream alternating palette with warm gold accent earns a base 4: atmospheric variation across slides (cream on odd, navy on even), italic-gold emphasis on key numbers is a recurring visual motif (slide-02, slide-06, slide-12), closing slide uses faint grid overlay for depth. Automatic −1 applied: a small gold dash appears below every section label throughout the deck (under 'THE QUARTER IN ONE LINE' slide-02, 'SEGMENT DETAIL' slide-03, 'EIGHT QUARTERS, $M' slide-04, and so on through all 12 slides) — decorative accent lines carrying no information. typographic_craft: The deck pairs tracked all-caps / small-caps labels ('NORTHWIND LOGISTICS', 'SEGMENT DETAIL', 'GROSS MARGIN BRIDGE') against a high-contrast editorial serif with a well-cut italic for display and body copy — a genuine two-face pairing. Weight contrast is strong: heavy display serif on headlines, regular weight for body annotations. Table columns on slide-03 and slide-08 carry right-aligned numerals. Hierarchy reads at a glance from across a room on every slide. No overflow, clipping, or container collision is visible anywhere. What prevents a 5: tabular figure usage is unverifiable at screenshot resolution, and the display scale is not optimized across slides of varying semantic weight (e.g., slide-11's two large figures receive the same treatment as slide-07's three, despite different informational density).

A high-quality serif face with real weight and style contrast is used throughout: tracked all-caps for category labels, heavy roman for action titles, italic gold for emphasis, display-size roman for KPI figures — four genuine levels of hierarchy legible at a glance (visible in slides 02, 06, 08). No default system stack. No overflow or clipping on any slide. What prevented 5: the headline on slide-02 runs approximately 90+ characters across nearly full width, well outside the 45–75 optimal measure. Minor register inconsistency: sub-labels on slide-07 and slide-05 render at the same apparent weight/size, collapsing two hierarchy levels.
hierarchy_density: Corpus 02 mandates action titles and reading-first density for an executive committee that will circulate the deck. Action-title check on slides 2–11 (the substantive content slides): all 10 assert a finding — slide-02 'Revenue reached $47.2M, up 12.4% — but gross margin compressed 180 bps', slide-06 'Top-10 share fell to 38% — a fourth consecutive quarter of decline', slide-09 'Fuel exposure is unhedged beyond Q1 FY27', etc. 100% asserting; no cap at 3 applies. Grouping is visual throughout (stat cards, two-column bridge panels, ruled tables). What prevents a 5: slide-07 carries only three stat figures and a one-clause subtitle with no explanatory body text, and slide-11 has just two metrics and no supporting context — both would struggle to stand alone without a presenter, drifting from the 'must stand alone when circulated' requirement in the brief.
